Subir Nandi Das, Advocate (In Person) With Md Abdul Alim Miah and Abdul Ouiyum Khan Advocates—For the Petitioner.

parties:
Subir Nandi Das ------- Petitioner [In Person)
vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Bangladesh Secretariat Dhaka and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
FRM Nazmul Ahasan, J: Upon an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh a Rule Nisi was issued in the following terms: 
"Supplementary-affidavit filed by the petitioner do form part of the main application. 
Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inaction of the respondents to preserve and display the portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Courtroom/Ejlash of the country shall not be declared illegal and without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 
The Rule is made returnable within 4(four) weeks from date. 
Pending hearing of the Rule, the respondents are directed to display and preserve the portrait of the Father of Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/Ejlash of the Country within 2 (two) months from date and to file an affidavit-in-compliance before this court within 2(two) months." 

2. Petitioner is a cautious citizen of Bangladesh and under constitutional obligation filed this application before this Court and the facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the preamble of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh contains the core elements of independent of Bangladesh and narrates it as "We, the people of Bangladesh, having proclaimed our independence on the 26th day of March, 1971 and through a historic struggle for national liberation, established the independent, sovereign people's Republic of Bangladesh,..." thereby glorifying the significance of liberation war and historic struggle for achieving the sovereignty of Bangladesh which was led by the founder father of the nation Bangabandha Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and only through the decade long struggle for independence against the then autocratic rule of Pakistan, finally resulting the independence of Bangladesh in 1971. 

3. It is stated that Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is a singular figure on the global stage and a man of quiet dignity and towering achievement, a giant for justice and a down-to-earth human inspiration. Many around the world were greatly influenced by his selfless struggle for human dignity, equality and freedom for the people of Bangladesh. His life was devoted to the service of his people and humanity, and he did so at great personal sacrifice. Remarkably, he emerged from around 14 years of detention to build a new country as golden Bangladesh based on his unswerving effort which resulted in liberation war and evolved an independent Bangladesh. Therefore, the utmost contribution and historic sacrifice of Bangabondhu shall harmoniously designate him as a national heritage and also a symbol of justice, freedom and national unity of Bangladesh. 

4. Thereafter, the emblem of freedom, independence, unity and prosperity of Bangladesh construed upon the entity of the father of nation and the ideology and spirit of Bangabondhu shall always remain alive as long this country exists in the world. The historic 7th March speech of the Father of the Nation has been recognized and included in the Memory of the World Inter-national Register, a list of world's important documentary heritage maintained by UNESCO. On March 7 in 1971, Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in his fiery speech called on the freedom-loving Bangalis to wage a decisive struggle against the Pakistani Rules. "এবারের সংগ্রাম আমাদের মুক্তির সংগ্রাম, এবারের সংগ্রাম স্বাধীনতার সংগ্রাম” Bangabandhu declared in a thunderous voice at a mammoth rally at the Racecourse Maidan (now Suhrawardy Udyan) that day. "প্রত্যেক ঘরে ঘরে দূর্গ গড়ে তোল। তোমাদের যা কিছু আছে তাই নিয়ে শত্রুর মোকাবেলা করতে হবে" The water-shed speech touched every Bangali heart across the then East Pakistan, now Bangladesh, and mobilised the whole nation to prepare for the ultimate sacrifice they made in the Liberation War and thereby it results an independent state as Bangladesh. 

5. Thereafter, the Bangabandhu is the greatest of all great Bangalees of all time, and Bangladesh achieved it' independence in 1971 under the sole leadership of Bangabandhu through a bloody war. He sacrificed his enter life for the emancipation of the people of Bangladesh, he spent almost 14 years in jail at different time of his life, and played the main role in every significant movement of nation such as language movement 1952, election of 1954, 6 points demand at 1966. People's revolution on 1969, general election on 1970, official declaration of independence on 26 March, 1971 and war of independence 1971, constitution of 1972. His contribution makes Bangladesh and Bangabandhu Synonymous. 

6. Thereafter, glorifying the significance of our founder father of state, Article 4A of the Constitution of the People Republic of Bangladesh has inserted in our constitution vide Fifteenth Amendment on 3-6-2011. The very Article of 4A of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh is reproduce as follows: 
"The portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman shall be preserved and displayed at the offices of the President, the Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Chief Justice and in head and branch offices of all government and semi-government offices, autonomous bodies, statutory public authorities, government and non-government educational institutions, embassies and missions of Bangladesh abroad" 

7. Thereafter, Article 4A was included within part-1 (The Republic) of the Constitution which is necessarily no limit to only the Chief officials or Head offices or the branches of executive but includes each and every government offices where public functions are carried out and the very object for insertion of said provision is to display and to preserve the portrait of Father of Nation is to pay tribute to the architect of independence. Being a grateful nation, the people of Bangladesh for showing their utmost respect and gratefulness towards the Bangabandhu, the parliament of Bangladesh which is the highest body of legislation constituted with the people mandate has been taken decision to preserve and display the portrait of Father of Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in the office of the President, the Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Chief Justice and in head and branch offices of all government and semi-government offices, autonomous bodies, statutory public authorities, government and non-government educational institutions, embassies and missions of Bangladesh abroad for remembrance his contribution, since the Bangabandhu is the symbol of national unity, strength and source of inspiration. 

8. Thereafter, the victory of Bangladeshi people from oppression and suppression of Pakistan has been achieved on 16th December 1971 and the father of the nation was released from Pakistan's Jail and on his return to his beloved country he initiated rebuilding a golden Bangladesh and in pursuance to that dream Bangabondhu formed a constitutional assembly with elected members to adopt and enact a constitution for the new born nation which was chaired by him. The Constitution establishes various branches of state and government including executive, judiciary and legislative. Furthermore, the Apex Court of the state was inaugurated and the founding stone was laid down by the father of the nation Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on 18th December, 1972 and the very day has been observing as "Supreme Court Day" in every year and, as such, in accordance with Article 4A of the Constitution, the Portrait of Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be preserved and displayed in each courtrooms of the country including the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh to uphold the dignity, prestige and nobility of the Hon'ble court itself and, as such, a direction may kindly be given to preserve and display the portrait of father of nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every court room/ejlash of the Country. 

9. It is evident from the plain reading of Article 4A that the legislative intension of insertion of this Article is to glorying the contribution of Bangabadhu towards dreaming an independent Bangladesh which is the basic elixir of our constitution and thereby display the portrait of the father of nation in all visible places inclusive to government offices where courtrooms are included within the preview of said Article as such the respondents shall be obliged by constitution to display and preserve the portrait of Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every courtroom in Bangladesh. 

10. The petitioner also filed a supplementary affidavit dated 28-8-2019 stating that the Order 11 of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) Rules, 1998 also described the Court room as office. Rule-I of Order II of the Rules, 1988 as follows: 
"1. Except during the vacation and on holidays and subject to any order of the Chief Justice, the office of the Court shall remain open daily from 8-00 am to 2-00 pm on week days. 
Provided that no matter, unless of an urgent nature, shall be received within one hour of the closing time." 

11. So, it appears from the aforesaid provision of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) Rules, 1998 that the Court rooms are the public office and, as such, the portrait of the father of the Nation should be preserved and displayed in every Courtroom/ Ejlash of the Country. 

12. In reply the respondent No.1 government filed an affidavit-in-compliance stated that after receiving the Order dated 29-8-2019 to issue Rule and the following direction:-  “……. The respondents are directed to display and preserve the portrait of the Father of Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/Ejlash of the Country within 2(two) months from date and to file an affidavit-in-compliance before this court within 2(two) months." 

13. The respondent No.1 vide memo No.10. 00.0000.129.18.12.19-1086 dated 23-9-2019 have instructed all the concerned office of the Lower Court authority to take necessary measures to hang the Portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at the Court Room/Ejlash. The Assistant Secretary, Law & Justice Division, Writ Section-1, vide memo No. 53/2019(Writ-1)-706 dated 30-9-2019 have requested the respondent No.1 to send the photo of the Portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman for the purpose of preserving the portrait in every Court Room and Ejlash of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. 

14. It is stated that Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (1920-1975) is the architect of independent Bangladesh and the father of the Nation of Bangladesh. He was the president of Bangladesh (in absentia from 26 March 1971 to 11 January 1972), Prime Minister of Bangladesh (1972-24 January1975), President of Bangladesh (25 January 1975-15 August 1975). 

15. It is stated that he was one of the principal organisers behind the formation of the East Pakistan Muslim Students League (est. 1948). His active political career began with his election to one of the posts of joint secretaries of the East Pakistan Awami Muslim League (1949). In 1953, he was elected general secretary of the East Pakistan Awami Muslim League, a post that he held until 1966 when he became president of the party. Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was a pragmatic politician. In the Pakistan state, he appeared as the undaunted advocate of the Bengali interests from the start. He was among the first language prisoners. However, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman grew in political eminence in the early 1960. Through his organizing ability Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was able to salvage the Awami League from a series of defections and exit of various factions from the mainstream party. He reorganized the Awami League and put it on a firm foundation. In 1966, he announced his famous six-point programmed, calling it 'Our [Bengalis'] Charter of Survival', which aimed at self-rule for East Pakistan. Struck sharp at the roots of West Pakistani dominance, the six-point programme at once drew the attention of the nation. Though conservative elements of all political parties looked at it with consternation, it instantaneously stirred the younger generation, particularly the students, youth and working classes. 

16. Being disturbed by the political views of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the Ayub regime put him behind bars. A sedition case, known as "Agartala Conspiracy Case" was brought against Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, but due to a mass uprising took place in his favour in early 1969 and Ayub administration was compelled to release him on 22 February 1969 unconditionally. On the following day of his release, the Sarbadaliya Chhatra Sangram Parishad (All Parties Students Action Committee) organised a mass reception to him at Ramna Race-Course (now, Suhrawardy Uddyan) and accorded him the title Tanga-bandhu' (Friend of the Bengalis). In Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, they saw a true leader who suffered jail terms for about fourteen years during the 23 years of Pakistani Rule. 

17. The general elections of December 1970 made Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman the sole spokesman of East Pakistan. The people gave him the absolute mandate in favour of his six-point doctrine. On 7 March, 1971, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman made a historic address at a mammoth gathering at the Race Course which marked a turning point in the history of the Bengali nation. In his address made specific charges against the Martial Law authorities which failed to transfer power to the elected representatives. At the end of his speech, he made a clarion call, saying: "Build forts in each homestead. You must resist the Pakistani enemy with whatever you have in hand. Remember, we have given a lot of blood, a lot more blood we shall give if need be, but we shall liberate the people of this country, Insha Allah [i.e., if God blessed]..The struggle this time is the struggle for our emancipation; the struggle this time is the struggle for independence." 

18. That, although during the War of Liberation begun in the wake of the 25 March 1971, army crackdown Bangabandhu had been a prisoner in the hands of Pakistan, he was made in absentia, the President of the provisional government, called the Mujibnagar Government, formed on 10 April 1971 by the people's representatives to head the Liberation War. He was also made the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. Throughout the period of the War of Liberation, Sheikh Mujib's charisma worked as the source of national unity and strength. After the liberation of Bangladesh on 16 December 1971 from Pakistani occupation, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was released from Pakistan jail and via London he arrived in Dhaka on 10 January 1972. 

19. Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman headed the first government of the post-liberation Bangladesh for a period of three years and a half. Starting from scratch, his government had to deal with the countless problems of a war ravaged country. Restoring law and order, rehabilating the mukhtijodhas, restoring the ruptured communication system, and most importantly, feeding the hungry millions and many other problems bedevilled his administration. Because of his charismatic leadership Bangladesh gained recognition from the international community. 

20. It is submitted that Article 150(2) under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh states as follows:- 
“যেহেতু এইরূপ বিশ্বাসঘাতকতামূলক আচরণের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে বাংলাদেশের. সাড়ে সাত কোটি মানুষের অবিসাংবাদিত নেতা বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান বাংলাদেশের জনগণের আত্মনিয়ন্ত্রণের আইনানুগ অধিকার প্রতিষ্ঠার লক্ষ্যে ১৯৭১ সনের ২৬শে মার্চ তারিখে ঢাকায় যথাযথভাবে স্বাধীনতার ঘোষণা প্রদান করেন এবং বাংলাদেশের জনগণের প্রতি উদাত্ত আহ্বান।" 

21. In view of the above stated proclamation, where the then undisputed leader of 75 million of people of Bangladesh, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, in due fulfillment of the legitimate right of self-determination of the people of Bangladesh, have made the courageous effort in declaring the independence of Bangladesh which subsequently have created the People's Republic of Bangladesh and hence the State along with all its office is indebted to Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and, as such, the display and preservation of the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/ejlash is a obligatory in terms of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

22. It is submitted that Article 150(2) under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh states as follows:- 
“যেহেতু আমরা বাংলাদেশের নির্বাচিত প্রতিনিধিগণ, বাংলাদেশের সর্বোচ্চ ক্ষমতার অধিকারী জনগণ কর্তৃক আমাদিগকে প্রদত্ত কর্তৃত্বের মর্যাদা রক্ষার্থে নিজেদের সময়ে যথাযথভাবে একটি গণপরিষদরূপে গঠন করিলাম, এবং পারস্পারিক আলোচনা করিয়া, এবং বাংলাদেশের জনগণের জন্য সাম্য, মানবিক মর্যাদা ও সামাজিক সুবিচার নিশ্চিত করণার্থে, সার্বভৌম গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রক্ষপে বাংলাদেশের প্রতিষ্ঠা ঘোষণা করিলাম এবং তদারা বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান কর্তৃক ইতিপূর্বে ঘোষিত স্বাধীনতা দৃঢ়ভাবে সমর্থন ও অনুমোদন করিলাম,”

23. In view of the above stated proclamation, where in order to ensure for the people of Bangladesh equality, human dignity and social justice, the elected representative of the then people of Bangladesh declare and constitute Bangladesh to be a sovereign People's Republic and thereby confirm the declaration of independence already made by Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Hence the proclamation of Independence signifies the importance of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in establishment of a sovereign state, as such, the display and preservation of the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/Ejlash is a tribute to the Father of the Nation.

24. It is submitted that Article 150(2) under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh states as follows:- 
“এতদ্বারা দৃঢ়ভাবে ঘোষণা ও সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিতেছি যে, সংবিধান প্রণীত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান প্রজাতন্ত্রের রাষ্ট্রপতি থাকিবেন এবং সৈয়দ নজরুল ইসলাম প্রজাতন্ত্রের উপ-রাষ্ট্রপতি থাকিবেন, এবং রাষ্ট্রপতি প্রজাতন্ত্রের সকল সশস্ত্র বাহিনীর সর্বাধিনায়ক হইবেন, ক্ষমা প্রদর্শনের ক্ষমতাসহ প্রজাতন্ত্রের সকল নির্বাহী ও আইন প্রণয়ন ক্ষমতা প্রয়োগ করিবেন, একজন প্রধানমন্ত্রী নিয়োগ এবং তাহার বিবেচনায় প্রয়োজনীয় অন্যান্য মন্ত্রী নিয়োগ ক্ষমতার অধিকারী হইবেন, কর আরোপণ ও অর্থ ব্যয়ন ক্ষমতার অধিকারী হইবেন, গণপরিষদ আহ্বান ও মুলতবীকরণ ক্ষমতার অধিকারী হইবেন, এবং বাংলাদেশের জনগণকে একটি নিয়মতান্ত্রিক ও ন্যায্যানুগ সরকার প্রদানের লক্ষ্যে প্রয়োজনীয় অন্যান্য সকল কায করিতে পারিবেন”
 
25. In view of the above stated proclamation, where the then elected representative of the peoples of Bangladesh, affirmed Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, as the President of the Republic of Bangladesh and vested all executive, legislative powers in his hand, including the power to summon and adjourn the constituent assembly, in order to give the people an order and just government symbolizes him as the sole person to ensure equality, human dignity and social justice, hence the display and preservation of the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/Ejlash is a tribute to the Father of the Nation. 

26. It is submitted that Article 4A of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh reads as follows:-
"The Portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman shall be preserved and displayed at the offices of the President, The Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Chief Justice and in head and branch offices of all government and semi-government and non-government educational institutions, embassies and missions of Bangladesh abroad." 

27. In furtherance of the mention of the Portrait of the Father of the Nation at the Constitution of Bangladesh, under section 3 of the জাতির পিতার প্রতিকৃতি সংরক্ষণ ও প্রদর্শন আইন-২০০১ states as follows:- 
জাতির পিতার প্রতিকৃতি সংরক্ষণ ও প্রদর্শন বাধ্যতামূলক ।-সকল সরকারী, সরকারী, স্বায়ত্তশাসিত প্রতিষ্ঠান, সংবিধিবদ্ধ সরকারী কর্তৃপক্ষের প্রধান ও শাখা কার্যালয় মিলনায়ন ও গ্রন্থাগার, শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান, বিদেশে অবস্থিত বাংলাদেশের দূতাবাস ও মিশনসমূহে এবং বিধি নির্ধারিত অন্যান্য কার্যালয় ও প্রতিষ্ঠানে বাধ্যতামূলকভাবে জাতির পিতার প্রতিকৃতি সংরক্ষণ ও প্রদান করিতে হইবেঃ
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, ধর্মীয় প্রতিষ্ঠানের ক্ষেত্রে এই ধারার বিধান শিথিলযোগ্য হইবে।

28. In substantiating the Article 4A of the Constitution, section 3 of the জাতির পিতার প্রতিকৃতি সংরক্ষণ ও প্রদর্শন আইন-২০০১, made it a mandatory provision to include the portrait of the father of the Nation at all institutions, except religious and worship places. Therefore, we, on behalf of the State also believe that Judiciary, being an institution under the Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh, is also under the mandatory provision to display and preserve the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every Court Room/Ejlash, as such we are also in support of the Rule and pray before your Lordships to make the Rule absolute. 

29. It is submitted that from the all above circumstances and legal explanation, each citizen, officials and institutions are bound to respect and must pay tribute to the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and from the moral duty and legal obligation, the state is supporting the Rule and humbly pray for making the Rule absolute. 

30. Mr Subir Nandi Das, learned Advocate appearing In Person submits that the word `Office' has been well defined in the Black Law Dictionary and as per the definition a Judicial `Office' is that which is related to the administration of justice. Since the court rooms has been established for the purpose of fulfilment of administration of justice, so the court room is a public office and as per the provision of Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be displayed and preserve in every court room of the country. The constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh for the purpose of administration of justice among the people of the country has established Supreme Court comprising High Court Division and Appellate Division and also established subordinate court around the country and from the court rooms/Ejlashs administration of justice is served to the litigants and court is called the last resort of the people, since the court rooms are the government office, it's the constitutional duty to preserve and displayed the portrait of Bangabandhu herein also. But unfortunately it appears that no portrait of father of nation is being displayed in any court room of Bangladesh which is the clear violation of the provision of Article 4A of the constitution and, as such, a direction may kindly be given to preserve and display the portrait of father of nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every court room/ejlash of the Country. 

31. The learned Advocate further submits that the victory of Bangladeshi people from oppression and suppression of Pakistan has been achieved on 16th December 1971 and the father of the nation was released from Pakistan's Jail and on his return to his beloved country he initiated rebuilding a golden Bangladesh and in pursuance to that dream Bangabondhu formed a constitutional assembly with elected members to adopt a constitution for the new born nation which was chaired by him. The Constitution establishes various branches of state and government including executive, judiciary and legislative. Furthermore, the Apex Court of the state was inaugurated and the founding stone was laid down by the father of nation Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on 18th December, 1972 and the very day has been observing as "Supreme Court Day" in every year and, as such, in accordance with Article 4A of the Constitution, the Portrait of Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be preserved and displayed in each courtrooms of the country including the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh to uphold the dignity, prestige and nobility of the Hon'ble court itself and, as such, a direction may kindly be given to preserve and display the portrait of father of nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every court room/ejlash of the Country. 

32. The learned Advocate further submits that it is evident from the plain reading of Article 4A that the legislative intension of insertion of this Article is to glorying the contribution of Bangabadhu towards dreaming an independent Bangladesh which is the basic elixir of our constitution and thereby display the portrait of the father of nation in all visible places inclusive to government offices where courtrooms are included within the preview of said Article as such the respondents shall be obliged by constitution to display and preserve the portrait of Bangabondu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every courtroom in Bangladesh. 

33. Mr Yousuf Hossain Humayun, learned Senior Counsel and also Vice-Chairman of Bangladesh Bar Council, in support of the argument advanced by the petitioner submits that after liberation war of our country Bangabondhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the father of the Nation inaugurated the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 18-12-1972 and now the very day has been observing as 'Supreme Court Day' in every year and, as such, in accordance with Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the patriot the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, should be preserved and displayed in every court room including the Supreme court of Bangladesh to uphold the dignity, prestige and nobility of the Hon'ble Court itself. 

34. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General along with Mr ABM Abdullah Al Mahmud, learned Deputy Attorney-General and Mohammad Saiful Alam, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the government-respondent supported the contention made in the affidavit-in-compliance and submits that in compliance of the court order dated 29-8-2019 the government has instructed all the appropriate authority to take necessary measures to hang the patriot of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at the court room/ejlash and assistant secretary of the Ministry of Law, have requested to the respondent No.1 to send photo patriot of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman for the purpose of preserve in every courtroom/ejlash in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. 

35. The learned Attorney-General submits that Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was a leader of the democratic movement against the Pakistan and the leader of language movement in 1952 and also a leader of non-cooperation movement which was the basis of Liberation War in 1971. Thereafter, he emerged as the leader of National Liberation War and declared Independence of Bangladesh on 26th March, 1971 under his leadership Bangladesh has emerged as a sovereign State. As such the founder Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be respected by all the citizen of Bangladesh as well as all the organ of this state including the judiciary. Thus the respondent No.1 after issuance the rule has taken immediate initiative to display the patriot of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every court room/ ejiash and accordingly the direction of this court is complied with. 

36. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and Mr Yousuf Hossain Humayun, learned Senior Counsel and Vice-president of Bangladesh Bar Council and Mr Mahbubey Alam learned Attorney-General on behalf of the respondents. 

37. The preamble of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh contains the core element of independent of Bangladesh and narrates it as "We, the people of Bangladesh, having proclaimed our independence o the 26th day of March, 1971 and through a historic struggle for national liberation, established the independent, sovereign People's Republic of Bangladesh." The historic struggle for National Liberation, establishment of independent sovereign state are all led by the founder Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman through his decade long struggle for independence against the then autocratic rule of Pakistan, finally resulting the independence of Bangladesh in 1971. 

38. The Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman sacrificed his entire life for the emancipation of the people of Bangladesh, he spent almost 14 years in jail at different time of his life, and played the main role in every significant movement of nation such as language movement 1952, Election of 1954, 6 point demand at 1966, People's revolution on 1969, general election on 1970, official declaration of independence on 26th March 1971 and war of independence 1971, Constitution of 1972. Those contribution makes Bangladesh and Bangabandhu Synonymous. Glorifying the significance of our founder father of state, Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh has inserted in our constitution vide "Fifteenth Amendment on 30-6-2011" The very Article of 4A of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh is reproduced as follows: "The portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, shall be preserved and displayed at the offices of the President, the Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Chief Justice and in head and branch offices of all government and semi-government offices, autonomous bodies, statutory public authorities, government and non-government educational institutions, embassies and missions of Bangladesh abroad." 

39. The word 'Office' has been well defined in the Black Law Dictionary and as per the definition a Judicial "Office" is that which is related to the administration of justice. Since the court rooms have been established for the purpose of fulfillment of administration of justice, so the court room is an 'office' and as per the provision of Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the portrait of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be displayed and preserved in every court room of the country. It further appears that after independence of Bangladesh the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh. Mujibur Rahman inaugurated the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 18th December, 1972 and the very day is being observed as "Supreme Court Day" in every year as such in accordance with Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the portrait of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman shall be preserved and displayed in each courtrooms of the country including the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh to uphold the dignity, prestige and nobility of the Supreme Court itself. 

40. It may be mentioned that in many country like USA, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, photographs of their national hero and father of the Nation and our neighbouring country India and Pakistan portrait of their Father of the Nation has been preserved in the court rooms. 

41. Moreover, many countries in the world have taken necessary measures to display the portrait of the father of the nation as glorifying their national heritage and independence. In many states of United States of America the courthouse contain the portrait of national heroes, in Vietnam. Cambodia and Laos the photographs of father of the nation of the respective countries are even being hung in every classrooms and even in court room of India and Pakistan the portrait of their father of nation has been preserved and displayed for showing respect to their father of nation and, as such, in pursuance to the Article 4A of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh displaying the portrait of father of nation at court rooms should be made mandatory for the sake of history and heritage of Bangladesh. 

42. In every country Father of the Nation is the symbol of national unity. In Bangladesh, Bangabandhu united the whole nation and lead the liberation war and under his leadership Bangladesh emerged as a sovereign state and he gave us the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, wherein judiciary is one of the main organ. Since the court rooms has been established for the purpose of fulfilment of administration of justice, so the court room is a public office and as per the provision of Article 4A of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the portrait of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman should be displayed and preserve in every court room of the country. For the purpose of administration of justice among the people the Constitution has established Supreme Court comprising High Court Division and Appellate Division and also established subordinate court around the country and from the court rooms/Ejlashs administration of justice is served to the litigants and court is called the last resort of the people, it was the constitutional duty of the government to preserve and display the portrait of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. But unfortunately it appears that no portrait of father of nation was displayed in any court room of Bangladesh which is inconsistent with the provision of Article 4A of the Constitution. 

43. However, an ad-interim order was passed on 29-8-2019 to preserve and display the portrait of Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in every court room/ejlash of the Country. 

44. It appears from the affidavit-in-compliance that after issuance of the Rue and the direction on 29-8-2019 the respondents have already complied the order of this court and the learned Attorney-General submits that the portrait of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman has been displayed in all court rooms of Bangladesh including Supreme Court of Bangladesh with full dignity. In this regard we appreciate the step taken by the government and the concern authority to comply with the Court's order immediately. 

45. However, in consideration of the facts and circumstances discussed above, we are of the view the Rule may be absolute. 

46. In the result the Rule is made absolute. 

Before parting with the case we would like to express our deep gratitude to the learned Advocates appearing in the case for their assistance to us.
